long_biography.plain_text:
Casino entrepreneur John Janshen chose familiar brewery executives when handing over daily management of Janshen-Hahnraths in 1996. He wanted managers who understood its informal working culture. The owners had been spending much of their time developing overseas markets; appointing a new executive team gave the expanding organisation more attention at home.

Staff participation had also shaped the company's new headquarters. Janshen invited employees to describe what they needed to work effectively, then commissioned three architectural practices to prepare designs. The chosen building replaced premises that repeated extensions had failed to keep large enough for the growing business.
